Climate & Environment.title: The expansion of Heathrow would be an expensive disaster for Britain and the world. Burnham needs to block it | George Monbiot
Climate & Environment.text:
A third runway would fly in the face of reason. If we are to prioritise human life over short-term ‘growth’, we need to use planes less, not more
 If a third runway is built at Heathrow, what will be the impact on the wealth of the nation? It will cost us somewhere between £23.4bn and £62.5bn. These are not my figures; they weren’t calculated by environmental groups, but by the Department for Transport.For decades, government ministers have told us that airport expansion is essential for “growth”. As chancellor, Rachel Reeves claimed that a third runway at Heathrow would add 0.43% to GDP, figures we later discovered came from a report commissioned by the airport. The transport department’s own analysis concluded that the real addition to GDP would be between 0.03% and 0.05%: eight to 14 times less. Against this, it weighed the social and environmental costs of the project, to reveal a massive net loss. It found that a third runway would cause major harm to the health and wellbeing of up to 3 million local people.George Monbiot is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

That approach reshaped the look of the model considerably. This new build lands between the two, adding protection through material choice alone while leaving the silhouette's design language untouched.It's a logical move for a shoe that has become one of the defining faces of Nike's mesh runner wave. Entertainment.title: Raymond Weil Expands Its Anniversary Story With the Limited-Edition Millesime Jubilee Watch
Entertainment.text: SummaryRaymond Weil marks its 50th anniversary with the millesime Jubilee chronograph.The 39mm steel watch features a light-blue bi-compax dial and RW5030 movement.Limited to 500 pieces, it is priced at $4,275 USD.Raymond Weil is continuing its 50th-anniversary celebrations with the new Millesime Jubilee, a limited-edition automatic chronograph that follows the ultra-exclusive The Fifty unveiled at Watches & Wonders earlier this year. Founded in Geneva in 1976, the independent, family-owned watchmaker has been revisiting its history throughout 2026 via its travelling Legacy Tour, and Jubilee translates the anniversary story into a more widely available proposition. Where The Fifty was restricted to 50 examples powered by restored, hand-decorated Valjoux 23-6 movements dating from 1976, Jubilee is limited to 500 pieces, carrying forward its predecessor’s neo-vintage design language within the contemporary millesime collection.The watch is housed in a 39mm stainless steel case measuring 12.9mm thick, with a sapphire glassbox crystal accentuating the layered construction of its light-blue dial. Two midnight-blue, azurage-finished subdials establish the bi-compax chronograph layout, complemented by a silver-toned chapter ring, textured central section and an applied “EST 1976” cartouche referencing the Maison’s founding year. Black hour markers and obelisk-shaped hour and minute hands feature green-glowing Super-LumiNova, while a midnight-blue calfskin strap completes the restrained color palette. Inside is the self-winding RW5030 chronograph calibre, delivering a 62-hour power reserve and visible through a sapphire caseback; the watch is also water-resistant to 50 meters.The millesime Jubilee was officially unveiled in Sydney, the seventh stop of Raymond Weil’s 2026 Legacy Tour, which will subsequently travel to Singapore and Paris as the brand’s anniversary program approaches its conclusion. Entertainment.title: ISSEY MIYAKE SS27 Is a Breath of Fresh Air
Entertainment.text: SummaryIssey Miyake's Spring/Summer 2027 collection, "Figure of Ma," interprets the Japanese idea of meaningful negative space as the air between fabric and body.Ballooning trench coats, plaster-inspired tops, mesh knit capris, signature pleated pieces and a Camper footwear collaboration all shift shape with the wearer, moving with the body rather than confining it.Built around “Ma”, the Japanese aesthetic concept of meaningful negative space between elements, Issey Miyake’s Spring/Summer 2027 collection interprets “Ma” as the air and space between fabric and the body. Satoshi Kondo, the Japanese house’s head designer and art director since 2019, debuted the latest collection, “Figure of Ma”, with an all-black set at the Judo Institute during Paris Fashion Week. The show opened in silence, with a single dancer draped in beige pleats, then a troupe introduced a giant cloud-like billowing fabric that unveiled a collection of sculptural yet featherlight tops, voluminous ultra-light outerwear that catches the wind, and vibrant signature pleats.The collection introduced rounded silhouettes, airy volumes, and surfaces that morphed with the wearer’s every movement. Each piece captured air and shifted shape with the wearer's movement — ballooning trench coats in purple and black, torso-molded plaster gauze-inspired sleeveless tops, textured mesh knit capris, a puffed-shoulder plisse skirt, and patterned pleated outerwear. Also revealed were buttery leather bags, floppy pleated headwear, and a footwear collaboration with Camper. Issey Miyake's “Figure of Ma” collection moves with the body rather than confining it. Sleeves and hems moved as the models did, billowing and deflating like breathing, taking a new form as fabric met the body, turning tailored silhouettes into dynamic expressions of “Ma”.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Saint Laurent Presents a Golden SS27 & NikeSKIMS Opens Shanghai Pop-up in This Week's Top Fashion News
Entertainment.text: SummaryGlobal retail footprints are expanding with NikeSKIMS and Ann Demeulemeester opening new physical destinations.High-profile collaborations dominated this week, including Zara x John Galliano, Zendaya x On, and Kader Sylla's adidas signature shoe.Saint Laurent's golden SS27 runway show fueled rumors of Anthony Vaccarello’s potential departure.Anthony Vaccarello Drapes Saint Laurent in Gold for SS27Anthony Vaccarello presented Saint Laurent’s Women’s Spring/Summer 2027 collection in Paris, taking over the Trocadéro beneath the Eiffel Tower. The runway show centered entirely on gold — a shade favored by Yves Saint Laurent — to reinterpret the house's archival codes. Vaccarello reimagined foundational archetypes like sahariennes, trench coats, and sharp tailoring through a monochromatic, metallic lens, utilizing materials from organza to gold-leaf-coated latex. The gilded theme extended to filigree accessories and snake-shaped heels before closing with dramatic black velvet tailoring. An intimate final moment, where Vaccarello handed a key to a young boy in the audience, sparked widespread industry speculation that the grand presentation signaled his official exit from the luxury house.NikeSKIMS Debuts First Physical Destination in China With Shanghai Pop-UpNike and SKIMS officially unveiled their joint venture's first physical destination in China. SKIMS Co-Founder Kim Kardashian hosted an early preview of the Shanghai HKRI Taikoo Hui Pop-Up ahead of its late-September opening. The retail space showcases the complete NikeSKIMS Fall Edit 01 collection, spanning apparel, footwear, and accessories. Designed to mirror the joint brand’s aesthetic, the layout integrates custom displays and dedicated lounge areas for try-ons. The Shanghai location also provides localized consumer services, including on-site tailoring. During the preview, Kardashian highlighted the Chinese market's importance for the label's next chapter and detailed her excitement over selecting the Rift as her debut sneaker silhouette. The pop-up remains open through February 2027.Zara and John Galliano Launch Debut "Re{form}" Vol. 1 CollectionZara and couturier John Galliano have officially launched their inaugural collaboration. Titled "Re{form}" Vol. 1, the genderless collection treats mass-market archival Zara garments as raw prototypes, dismantling and reconstructing them using high-fashion couture techniques. Acting as a creative exchange between Zara's history and the former Maison Margiela creative director, the lineup features unexpected silhouettes inspired by post-Revolutionary France, film noir, and traditional gardening attire. Key transformations include oversized button-up shirts foil-printed to mimic leather coats, lace shift dresses repurposed into ruffled collars, and multi-layered dresses engineered to create the illusion of structured outerwear. Accompanied by a campaign shot by Steven Meisel, the debut drop is available now on Zara’s webstore.Ann Demeulemeester Opens Paris Flagship Store at the Palais RoyalAnn Demeulemeester expanded its permanent physical footprint, opening a new 150-square-meter Paris boutique situated in the historic Jardin du Palais Royal. The store marks the label's second major retail debut of the year, following a recent Milan opening. Operating as a unified destination for the brand, the minimalist, grayscale space houses menswear, womenswear, footwear, accessories, and the label's Serax tableware collection side by side. To celebrate the opening, the brand produced a limited-edition shirt that casts a signature house design as a collectible item. The Palais Royal boutique is part of a tightly edited global retail strategy, paving the way for upcoming flagship locations in London, Tokyo, and a shop-in-shop in Shanghai slated for 2027.Zendaya and On Unveil Second Co-Created Apparel and Footwear CollectionOn and Zendaya have released their second co-created footwear and apparel collection. Developed alongside longtime stylist Law Roach, the capsule fuses On's performance tech with signature styling, highlighted by an action-film-inspired campaign directed by Pantera. The apparel introduces an all-over custom python print on bodysuits and anoraks, alongside customizable oversized crew necks and sweatpants featuring adjustable bungee cords. A major highlight of the drop is the debut of the Cloudnova Moon, a Mary Jane-inspired low-profile sneaker that pairs an engineered knit upper with speed laces for versatile comfort. Arriving in three distinct colorways, the collection launched globally in early October across On's retail stores and special pop-up spaces in Los Angeles, Paris, Tokyo, and Chengdu.Kader Sylla Unveils First Signature Shoe With adidas SkateboardingProfessional skater Kader Sylla debuted his first-ever signature sneaker with adidas Skateboarding. Dubbed "The Kader," the mid-top model draws design cues from '90s adidas Equipment basketball silhouettes while updating the functionality for skate performance. Engineered for versatility, the sneaker launched in two suede colorways—brown with yellow snake stripes and black with purple speckled stripes. Breaking from tradition, the silhouette integrates the Three Stripes directly into the lacing system. Designed to handle heavy impact, the shoe incorporates a durable cupsole, a full-length Lightmotion midsole, and Adituff underlays. Sylla kicked off a global tour to celebrate the release, bringing demos and skateshop appearances to communities across North America. The signature model is currently available through adidas.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: LOEWE Distills a Sporty Spanish Summer for SS27
Entertainment.text: SummaryLOEWE’s SS27 collection delivers wearable, sport-forward apparel emphasizing slick materials, subtle logos, and a bold summer color palette.Standouts include jackets with metallic collars, scuba-style moccasins, and trousers with logos on the flies.At a purpose-built set at Château de Vincennes, Jack McCollough and Lazaro Hernandez presented their third LOEWE collection on October 2. Against the stark white backdrop, the clean yet energetic SS27 collection unfurled, refining their colorful, sport-forward vision of the Spanish label. Across the board, LOEWE introduced a highly wearable lineup characterized by slick materials, a bold summer color palette, and subtle yet interesting logo placements. Rather than ornamentation, the textiles and colors are what made these looks stand out. Minty green, yellow, blue, and red-orange dominated the overall color spectrum of the collection, while summer stripes and florals brought occasional texture. On several looks, where one would expect a leather or corduroy collar, there’s instead a metallic collar with exuberant gradients of orange and blue, matching wrap-style sunglasses styled throughout the show.  Other outerwear styles continued to the sport-oriented aesthetic of the previous collections, as seen in a number of shell jackets, utility coats, and anoraks. Notably, small LOEWE tags were sewn onto the flies of pants, offered in turquoise, gray, red, and olive. Discreet LOEWE logos also appeared on the toe box of new scuba-style moccasins, offered in a selection of colors like tan, black, pink, and yellow. The aquatic theme continues in a range of branded leather caps resembling swimming caps.Joining the logo trousers were some more unconventional pant styles featuring blooming flies, flaring out above the waist. The trousers were a bridge to the more revealing looks in womenswear: an ultra-mini leather dress, sheer spaghetti-strap dresses rolled up to the chest, and sheer tank dresses, made in layers of blue, yellow, and red-orange. The show closed with some of the most ornamental pieces, including boucle mini dresses and hotpants with frayed floral embroidery.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Streetsnaps: How Gia Seo Turns the Everyday Target Bag Into Her Main Character Accessory
Entertainment.text: In the landscape of modern styling, few creatives command color, texture, and unexpected proportion quite like Gia Seo. As a creative director, wardrobe stylist, and resident maximalist in New York City, Seo has built a reputation for turning outfit assembly into an art form. Known for her expressive, narrative-first aesthetic, she treats personal style as a continuous conversation between high-end design and everyday utility.Stepping onto the streets of Manhattan, Seo effortlessly integrates Target’s iconic bullseye reusable bag into two distinct, everyday looks. In her first outfit, she leans into classic city tailoring with a twist, pairing a KBB by KAHLANA belted trench coat with a pleated, mixed-pattern plaid midi skirt and sharp black leather boots. Rather than treating the vibrant red-and-white bag as an afterthought, she wears it slung over her shoulder as a graphic anchor that breaks up traditional autumnal tones.For her second look, Seo pivots to a more relaxed, downtown energy. She styles the KBB by KAHLANA low-rise jeans alongside an embroidered cream button-up detailed with black rosettes, accessorizing with studded platform clogs, slim sunglasses, and a green pepper keychain hooked to her belt loop. Here, the red bag acts as a bold pop of color against neutral denim, proving how easily a hyper-functional bag can double as a deliberate statement piece when layered into a well-curated fit.For Seo, a bag’s true value lies in how seamlessly it moves through the chaos of a full city day. Whether she’s carrying fabric swatches between studio visits, grabbing morning coffee, or hauling afternoon market pickups, the canvas bag shifts from pure utility to style component without missing a beat. It’s an approach to dressing that mirrors her broader design philosophy: high-impact style doesn't require overthinking, but just takes the right piece caught in the act of living.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Art & Culture.title: Salman Toor Paints the Highs and Lows of Queer Nightlife at London’s Courtauld Gallery
Art & Culture.text: SummaryNew York-based Pakistani-American artist unveils his first European solo at Courtauld Gallery in London, open until January 10, 2027The exhibition comprises 19 paintings focused on human connection and belonging, seen through his queer, brown protagonistsMaking his European debut, Pakistani-American painter Salman Toor lands in London for Someone Like You, his new solo exhibition at the Courtauld Gallery. Featuring 19 of his most iconic works, the presentation gives Britain a deservedly momentous introduction to Toor, who the New York Times dubbed “one of the most fascinating painters of his generation.”For the past decade, the New York-based artist has been redrawing narratives around immigration, desire, and power, placing queer brown men at the center of their own stories. Though the characters are fictional, Toor roots them in his own memories, imbuing them with a diaristic intimacy.But the works are more than odes to queer joy. They “inhabit the tension between intimacy and exposure, belonging and estrangement,” he said. “What it means to find a community, but also the daily costs associated with visibility”. Just as quickly as we succumb to the buzz of Toor’s sumptuously painted club scenes, so lively you can almost hear it, we retreat, with his protagonists, into quieter vignettes of alienation and estrangement. Toor manages a mastery of both the thrills of a night out and its aftermath, awake in the loneliest hours of the night.Zeroing in on human connection through hazy figures, distinctly their own while bleeding into one another. More than they are glamorous, they’re real, caught between the desire to belong while still trying to understand how to feel at home. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Courtauld (@courtauld)Someone Like You is now on view in London until January 10, 2027.Courtauld GallerySomerset House, Strand,London, WC2R 0RNClick here to view full gallery at Hypebeast
